title: Grateful Dead Live at Oregon State University on 1970-01-17
lineage: SBD > MR > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Clear soundboard capture brings out a soaring Dark Star‑St Stephen sequence and solid jams, making this winter‑70 show a standout despite occasional tape hiccups.
ai_review.review: The recording is a decent‑to‑good soundboard source that generally sounds clear, though listeners note some hiss, brief cuts and missing seconds. Musically the concert shines with an epic Dark Star → St Stephen → The Eleven stretch, strong renditions of Mason’s Children, High Time and Good Lovin’, and a second set that balances jam flights with ballads. Overall the performance is praised as one of the better winter‑70 shows, with only minor song‑specific gripes.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and highlight exceptional Dark Star/St Stephen jams; recording quality is consistently described as decent/good with only occasional issues, yielding a strong combined score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear and balanced; natural bass resonance from the venue noted. Some reviewers mention hiss, brief drop‑outs or missing seconds, but overall the tape is listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid winter‑70 set with a jam‑heavy second half; the Dark Star → St Stephen → The Eleven sequence anchors the show, while ballads and tighter numbers like High Time provide balance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is praised for being front‑and‑center with a crisp SG tone throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh’s bass is noted in tight jam moments (e.g., simultaneous launch with Jerry).
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen on keyboards receives enthusiastic mentions; uncertainty about Tom Constanten’s presence is expressed.
